articles.title: Melissa Barrera Says She Would Return to ‘Scream’ Franchise If the Rights ‘Were Ever to Leave’ Spyglass: ‘I Had an Amazing Time Making Those Movies’
articles.summary: Despite being fired from the “Scream” franchise in 2023, Melissa Barrera has made it clear that her real issue is with Spyglass Media Group, not the films themselves. When asked if she’d ever return for a future “Scream” film during a recent JustWatch interview, the actress responded, “not with the…
body: Barrera’s comments pertain to the company’s claim that she was acting antisemitically when she shared social media posts criticizing Israel amid the war in Gaza. At the time, Spyglass had said that it had “zero tolerance for antisemitism or the incitement of hate in any form, including false references to genocide, ethnic cleansing, Holocaust distortion or anything that flagrantly crosses the line into hate speech.”

Barrera continued, “Even with an apology, I wouldn’t go back to work with them. So, not that I’m holding my breath. I don’t think they have that ability. But if the franchise were ever to leave those hands and go into hands that I think honor Wes Craven’s legacy more, I think yeah.”

The “In the Heights” actress had starred in 2022’s “Scream” and that year’s “Scream VI” before she was ousted from the franchise. “Scream 7” was released earlier this year. Recently, she spoke about how “beautiful” she found the support around Macklemore to be following his removal from Ed Sheeran’s tour for his support of Palestine.

articles.title: Hayley Kiyoko Wants to Make a Lesbian ‘Pirates of the Caribbean’: ‘Keira Knightley, But Gay’
articles.summary: Hayley Kiyoko wants to sail the same-sex-loving high seas. The musician, novelist and filmmaker says her dream project is a queer take on “Pirates of the Caribbean.” “I would love to do a lesbian pirate show or movie — Keira Knightley, but gay,” she said.
body: The 'Girls Like Girls' director and fellow queer filmmakers Angela Robinson, Adam Shankman and Wash Westmoreland reveal their dream projects.

She’s hoping to turn her second novel, “Where There’s Room for Us,” into a film as well. “It’s a period piece, which no one wants to pay for, but they will one day,” she said to cheers and applause from the audience.

Adam Shankman, whose directorial credits include “Hairspray,” “Rock of Ages,” “Stop! That! Train!” and the upcoming Arnold Schwarzenegger and Alan Ritchson holiday action comedy “The Man With the Bag,” said his dream project is a big-screen adaptation of “ Spring Awakening,” the Tony Award-winning coming-of-age rock musical set in late 19th-century Germany.

Although he doesn’t think it could ever get the go-ahead because of its intense subject matter, “where terrible things happen to these kids,” Shankman said, “I think it is such a beautiful poem and it is such a beautiful story and it lives in me in such a haunting and beautiful way. I know exactly what I would do with it, and I know exactly how I would do it. I see it completely, and I would love to make it more than any other movie. If that was my last movie, I’d be fine.”

The musician, novelist and filmmaker says her dream project is a queer take on “Pirates of the Caribbean.
“I would love to do a lesbian pirate show or movie — Keira Knightley, but gay,” she said.
“It’s a period piece, which no one wants to pay for, but they will one day,” she said to cheers and applause from the audience.

The director’s sequel to 2023’s blockbuster “Godzilla Minus One” wowed journalists with epic thrills and the first R-rated action set…
body: “Takashi Yamazaki’s made a worthy successor to ‘Minus One’ with a family-centric story that’s also filled with thrilling action sequences and jaw-dropping monster battles,” adds Marissa Hill. “But it works in the quieter moments too… It’s still astonishing to me that these films, made on a fraction of the budget as current day blockbusters, look this good… the King of Monsters has never looked or sounded this grand.”

articles.title: ‘Paper Tiger’ Makes Its Case at NYFF Premiere: “A Labor of Love”
articles.summary: The James Gray film made its North American premiere to a warm reception on Friday evening, standing out as the kind of American indie that’s harder than ever to get made.
body: There are worse ways to be introduced, when you’re about to unveil your new film as the Opening Night selection of the New York Film Festival, than as “one of the great living American filmmakers.” But that’s exactly what Artistic Director Dennis Lim said as he brought Paper Tiger director to the stage at Lincoln Center’s Alice Tully Hall on Friday evening.

The general feelings around Paper Tiger feel distinct from Gray’s past films as well. Although a consistent critical darling, the Queens native hasn’t been able to break into the Oscar race in his career thus far, and at this point seems overdue — certainly, it wasn’t hard to think so hearing Lim’s comments framing the relaunch of Paper Tiger, which has not screened publicly since its world premiere in Cannes. The film had been widely acclaimed on the Croisette, and despite the jury overlooking the drama — as has, frustratingly, been a pattern for Gray’s movies at the festival over decades — it was being primed to roar with its fall launch by distributor Neon.

articles.title: Zurich Summit Game Changer Glen Basner and Edward Berger Reminisce on a Wild ‘Conclave’ Ride
articles.summary: Former Good Machine colleagues treated Zurich Summit attendees to behind-the-scenes anecdotes about making Berger's Vatican-set drama and touched on a busy year for award recipient Basner.
body: Quite the bromance unfolded on stage at the Zurich Film Festival Summit as Oscar-winning filmmaker Edward Berger held a session with FilmNation Entertainment founder and CEO Glen Basner, who is this year’s Game Changer award recipient.

“Glen, I’m so proud to have had the opportunity to make a film with you. I’m so happy to know you. I’m so happy to call you a friend, and I want to congratulate you on your wonderful career, for all the great movies, for all the filmmakers that you’ve inspired, that you’ve instilled confidence in,” said Berger after an hour-long discussion in which the two reflected on their time together, a chaotic film climate, and why great storytelling will always be at the heart of Basner’s work.

At this year’s Zurich Film Festival, Basner is producing three movies in the lineup: Florian Zeller’s Bunker with Javier Bardem and Penélope Cruz, A Talent for Murder with Helen Mirren and I Play Rocky, which proved a real crowd-pleaser at TIFF.

articles.title: Star Trek: Strange New Worlds Season 4 Finale Title Pays Homage To An All-Time Classic Episode
articles.summary: Star Trek: Strange New World's Season 4 finale title nods to a classic Next Generation episode name, but there are integral differences between the two stories.
body: The final episode of the fourth season of "Star Trek: Strange New Worlds" is called "Tomorrow's Enterprise." The story surrounds the eerie temporal mechanics of a colossal negative space wedgie that allows Uhura (Celia Rose Gooding) to communicate with herself one year in the future. Uhura learns that, in the future, her beloved boyfriend Scotty (Martin Quinn) has died in an accident, so the two Uhuras have to collaborate, across time, to save his life.

The title of the episode is also a fun callback to one of the most famous episodes of "Star Trek: The Next Generation," "Yesterday's Enterprise." Trekkies will clock this right away. Of course, "Tomorrow's Enterprise" is about saving one life and enjoying the halcyon warmth of a crew that loves each other. The season ends with teary speeches, hugs, and enjoyable group dinners. "Yesterday's Enterprise," meanwhile, is a dark tale of war and sacrifice full of blood, injury, and death. It's still a time-travel story, but tonally, the episodes couldn't be more different.

articles.title: YouTube and Meta Reverse Course, Will Accept ‘Musk’ Trailer Ad
articles.summary: The Google unit says the ad was "temporarily restricted" while Meta calls it "an error." TikTok and X remain silent.
body: Following an outcry over potential suppression, YouTube and Meta are changing direction on an ad for an Elon Musk documentary.

Bleecker Street, the studio behind Alex Gibney’s upcoming Musk, will be allowed to buy an ad for the trailer on the platform after all, a YouTube spokesperson tells The Hollywood Reporter. The trailer “was temporarily restricted by our system. Following review, the ad has been cleared to run,” the company said, also posting the message to social media.

On Friday, THR reported that YouTube, along with Meta, TikTok and X had all refused to allow Bleecker Street to run a paid ad for the trailer, raising the specter of suppression on a documentary about the very subject. The trailer had been released Thursday ahead of the film’s Oct. 9 release.

A YouTube spokesperson said the ad should be appearing soon, though as of late Saturday morning Bleecker Street has not yet been informed of any change. The company had been appealing the initial ruling from YouTube.

articles.title: Jonathan Lipnicki on His Bold Role Opposite Robert Pattinson in ‘Primetime’ and Why He Left L.A.
articles.summary: The former child star — famous for telling Tom Cruise "a human head weighs eight pounds" in 'Jerry Maguire' — opens up about baring all in the Lance Oppenheim-directed film, being brave and staying stubborn for what he loves most: "I don't quit."
body: A little more than a year ago, Jonathan Lipnicki started praying nightly for clarity in his career.

It worked. Not long after, Lipnicki arrived at a new gig, and while it didn’t deliver the most amount of screen time in his lengthy IMDb credits, it offered the boldest turn of the 35-year-old’s career. Lipnicki — a beloved child star who, at age 6, hit the jackpot by making his debut opposite Tom Cruise and Renée Zellweger in Cameron Crowe’s Jerry Maguire before moving on to other hits like Stuart Little — snagged a part in Lance Oppenheim ‘s Primetime for A24.

That applies to Lipnicki, who shed more than that — specifically, his pants — for a full frontal scene complete with a can of whipped cream. “As actors, we pray for dark material and for things we can really sink our teeth into. At the end of the day, you have to ask yourself, ‘Am I as courageous an artist as I say I am?’ I had to answer that question, and I was courageous enough to take the plunge,” Lipnicki told The Hollywood Reporter over Zoom in September. “I’ve tried to live by the idea that, when it comes to art, if something scares you, most likely you should do it.”

articles.title: Before Gilligan's Island, Russell Johnson Was In A Western Series With A Unique Plot
articles.summary: Russell Johnson's assorted pre-Gilligan's Island projects included this 1950s Western TV series about a gunfighter who becomes a lawyer.
body: Before playing Professor Roy Hinkley on "Gilligan's Island," Russell Johnson made the Western TV show rounds. At one point, that led to him co-starring on the lesser-known series "Black Saddle," which, though it lasted only two seasons, boasted some impressive guest stars and a unique premise: a gunfighter who becomes a lawyer.

It's sort of funny to think that Johnson received a purple heart for being shot down over a tropical island in World War II, yet he's mostly remembered for creating zany inventions as The Professor on a fictional tropical island. Considering how popular Sherwood Schwartz's "Gilligan's Island" was, though, it couldn't really have been any different. After all, stories of wartime heroism don't get massive syndication deals that ensure they permeate pop culture for generations to come. Unapologetically silly sitcoms like "Gilligan's Island," however, very much do.

articles.title: DC Boss James Gunn Addresses Lanterns' Most Controversial Decision
articles.summary: Lanterns Season 1's boldest choice has ruffled some feathers, prompting DC Studios head James Gunn to weigh in on the matter.
body: DC Studios co-head James Gunn has weighed in on the most controversial decision made in "Lanterns" Season 1 so far. The series, which plays like "True Detective" meets "Watchmen," is DC's riskiest bet yet. And while "Lanterns" has been met with a lot of acclaim, it's also not without its perceived issues. Namely, the death of one of the show's most important characters.

"Lanterns" follows Lantern Corps recruit John Stewart (Aaron Pierre) and Green Lantern legend Hal Jordan (Kyle Chandler), two intergalactic cops drawn into a mystery on Earth as they investigate a murder in the American heartland. Spoilers, but Hal Jordan dies in the first episode (specifically, in the show's 2026 timeline). That "Lanterns" Episode 1 twist ending raised all sorts of questions about the DC Universe, but it ruffled more than a few feathers in the process.
